newsitem.title: CHINA: China's new treasury note makes weak debut.
newsitem.headline: China's new treasury note makes weak debut.

text.p: China's latest three-year treasury note, debuting on the Shanghai stock exchange on Monday, opened at 98.00 yuan against a face value of 100 yuan, indicating weak demand, traders said.

Traders said the note, maturing in May 2000, sold slowly during its issue in May mainly due to a low coupon rate of 9.18 percent compared with an average yield of more than 10 percent for existing spot state debt contracts on the Shanghai bourse.

A total of 40 billion yuan worth of the three-year tradeable treasury note was issued in May. By the end of its issue on May 31, underwriters in Shanghai had sold less than 60 percent of the new T-note, industry sources said.

"The weak debut was expected because of the slow sales during the issue," said one trader. "But after its low opening, the yield of the new note has been raised to around 10.1 percent and potential for further falls is limited."
Traders said they expected the note to move around the current level for the rest of session on Monday.
They said the low opening had hit market sentiment on the spot market and could depress prices of other contracts.
"The weak demand of the new note has indicated a lack of liquidity for the spot state debt market," said a second trader.
"The booming stock markets and many new (domestic) A share issues will continue to suck money out of the spot market, depressing prices of the state debt contracts," he said.
